book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: Does the November 20, 2026 tape support buying at $484.52, or must new capital wait for support?

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the tape. Fundamentals tell you what to own; the stage of the trend tells you when to deploy.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.html: Broad US market conditions deteriorated sharply into November 20, 2026. Our market-facts ledger flags a confirmed Downtrend regime on the S&P 500 with 10 distribution days over 25 sessions. Only 38.8% of tracked leaders hold above their 50-day SMA, 46.9% sit above their 200-day SMA, and zero of nine sectors trade above their 20-day moving average. On November 20 alone, QQQ plunged -5.67% to $608.45 on 2.59x average volume (daily RSI 26.63), sliding further below both its 50-DMA ($710.96) and 200-DMA ($683.06).

Inside that market selloff, MSFT ($484.52) broke down from its prior Stage 2 coil into a confirmed Weinstein Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) with 7 institutional distribution days over 25 sessions. Both the market-facts ledger (Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback)) and the TradingView snapshot (STAGE_3) agree on the stage classification. Shares dropped -2.77% on November 20 (-6.78% 1W per TradingView; -7.51% 1W per Finviz) on 47.19 million shares, or 1.78x 30-day average volume. Price now sits -6.79% (-2.15 ATR) below its 50-day SMA ($519.84), -4.95% below its 10-week EMA ($509.73), and below Pivot S1 ($505.67) and Pivot S2 ($489.43).

Multi-timeframe oscillators show downside momentum has not yet turned up. On the weekly (1W) chart, MSFT stays +4.87% above its rising 30-week SMA ($462.01) and +9.22% above its 200-day SMA ($443.63), with weekly RSI neutral at 50.51. On the daily (1D) chart, RSI dropped to 34.76 while ATR14 expanded to $16.41 and Bollinger Bandwidth widened to 13.12%. On the intraday 4-hour (4H) chart, price ($484.52) sits well below the 4H EMA20 ($511.45) and 4H SMA50 ($524.58) with 4H RSI oversold at 27.36 and intraday_4h_turn = false.

web_blocks.title: 8.2 Support Shelf Audit, Stop Ratchet & Options Overlay (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE)

web_blocks.html: Reconciling the deterministic technical table is essential here. Because the automated snapshot scanner anchored nearest_support to the 50-day SMA ($519.84), its raw output lists a support_buy_zone of $502.08–$527.64—now overhead resistance above $484.52. With Pivot S2 ($489.43) breached, true downside support sits at the $462.00–$476.00 structural shelf, anchored by the rising 30-week SMA ($462.01) just beneath the 63-day swing low ($481.03). That tightened watch shelf delivers a 2.88:1 technical support-zone R:R to our $540.00 Base target against our ratcheted hard stop at $453.81 (30-week SMA $462.01 minus 0.5x ATR14 of $16.41, ratcheted upward from prior $452.41).

Our options engine assigns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE on MSFT as of November 20, 2026. The benchmark $480/$540 bull call debit spread costs $27.17 for a $32.83 maximum gain—a 1.21:1 reward-to-risk ratio below our 1.25:1 minimum hurdle. Because macOS Chrome automation is unavailable in this Linux environment, Robinhood and TradingView browser sessions were not queried, and public options chains govern this stand-aside call. Both equities and options wait for confirmed stabilization before committing fresh capital.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Why Gap-Through Discipline Matters in Stage 3
paragraphs: With 7 MSFT distribution days inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, a broken 50-DMA ($519.84), and an unconfirmed 4H RSI of 27.36, delayed two-day stop confirmations invite gap-through slippage. Any existing position must use an unconditional single-close or intraday breach stop at $453.81, while new capital waits patiently inside $462.00–$476.00.

web_blocks.html: The contrast with one week earlier underscores why position management rules never rely on static views. On November 13, MSFT held a tight 7.47% volatility squeeze above $519.00. Seven days later, 1.78x selling volume erased both the 50-day SMA and Pivot S2. Right-sizing existing exposure and keeping new cash sidelined until the 4H turn arrives prevents turning a normal pullback into an unhedged drawdown.

book_paragraphs: Even the finest software monopoly on earth can inflict months of pain if you buy it while institutional money is actively selling into a falling market. As of November 20, 2026, the broader US market tape is flashing unambiguous caution. Our market ledger shows the S&P 500 in a confirmed Downtrend with ten distribution days over twenty-five sessions. Not a single major sector sits above its 20-day moving average, and the Nasdaq-100 ETF QQQ plunged 5.67 percent on November 20 to $608.45 on more than two-and-a-half times normal volume.

Against that heavy macro wave, Microsoft's chart shifted out of its early-November volatility squeeze. Closing at $484.52 on 1.78 times 30-day average volume with seven stock-specific distribution days over 25 sessions, Microsoft sits in Weinstein Stage 3—a topping or pullback phase—6.8 percent below its 50-day moving average at $519.84 and nearly 5 percent below its 10-week exponential moving average at $509.73. Both weekly and daily pivots at $505.67 and $489.43 gave way during the week.

Look across all three timeframes—weekly, daily, and four-hour—and you see why patience pays. On the weekly chart, Microsoft still holds 4.87 percent above its rising 30-week average at $462.01 and 9.22 percent above its 200-day moving average at $443.63, with weekly RSI sitting at 50.5. That tells us the long-term primary trend has bent, not broken. Yet on the daily chart, RSI dropped to 34.76, and on the four-hour chart, RSI is buried at 27.36 with price well below the 20-period four-hour exponential average at $511.45 and no upward turn confirmed.

Notice one subtle discrepancy in our automated scanner output that every disciplined investor should catch. Because the mechanical screen anchored nearest support to the 50-day moving average at $519.84, it generated a theoretical support band of $502.08 to $527.64—which now sits overhead as resistance rather than below the $484.52 price. Real structural support lies lower, right on the rising 30-week average at $462.01 up to $476.00. Defining our actionable watch shelf at $462.00 to $476.00 gives new capital a 2.88-to-1 technical reward-to-risk ratio toward our $540.00 Base target against our ratcheted $453.81 stop.

Just below that shelf sits our non-negotiable line in the sand. Our prior structural stop sat at $452.41. Under our upward-only stop ratchet rule, we tighten that structural stop modestly higher to $453.81—anchored half an ATR below the rising 30-week moving average and safely clear of the 200-day moving average at $443.63. And because waiting for two consecutive closes in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend risks nasty gap-through slippage, our $453.81 stop is an unconditional single-close or intraday trigger.

We also checked the listed options market for stock-replacement or spread opportunities. Using public chains—since automated desktop browser sessions are offline in this Linux environment—our deterministic engine flags NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. A standard $480/$540 bull call spread costs $27.17 for a maximum $32.83 gain, offering just 1.21-to-1 reward-to-risk below our 1.25-to-1 floor. When neither the four-hour chart nor the options pricing offers an edge, standing aside with fresh capital is the highest-conviction move.

Before committing fresh dollars, we need to see one of two clear footprints on the chart. Either Microsoft tests the $462.00 to $476.00 support band, shakes out weak hands, and prints a four-hour higher low with four-hour RSI climbing back above 40, or buyers step in with heavy accumulation to reclaim the 50-day average near $519.84. Until one of those signals appears, patience protects our capital.

Also look closely at volume and distribution behavior across Microsoft's chart over the past five weeks. Seven institutional distribution days in twenty-five sessions—capped by November 20's 47.19 million share decline at 1.78 times normal volume—show large funds trimming exposure rather than quietly absorbing supply. Until those heavy-volume down days dry up and accumulation volume returns on upside sessions, respecting the CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT gate keeps you out of premature bottom-fishing.
